Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.

The Community You Will Join

The Global Threat Assessment Program (GTAP) provides 24/7 investigations and behavior-based threat assessments to guide Airbnb's response to ongoing critical safety incidents. Working across three regions (AMER, EMEA, and APAC), GTAP responds to ongoing threats of violence, stalking, harassment, and other serious safety incidents, partnering closely with Law Enforcement Operations, Legal, and Customer Support to mitigate threats to our platform and communities.

The Difference You Will Make

The Regional Operations Manager for the GTAP is responsible for overseeing day-to-day operations within their assigned region. This role is crucial in ensuring the safety and security of Airbnb's community within the region. You will lead a regional team of threat assessment managers, set and manage team performance expectations, and serve as the expert voice on high-threat incident deescalations.

A Typical Day

· Oversee the daily operations of the GTAP within the assigned region, ensuring alignment with Airbnb’s mission and vision.

· Manage threat assessment cases end-to-end within the region: triage incoming reports, investigations and structured threat assessments, develop incident management plans, and drive cases to resolution.

· Maintain rigorous case documentation in accordance with GTAP standards — every decision must be explainable, consistent, and auditable.

· Maintain regional situational awareness: track developing situations, and ensure relevant information reaches the appropriate GTAP and GSRM stakeholders in a timely way.

· Coordinate with the Global Operations Manager and other Regional Operations Managers to ensure consistency and effectiveness across all regions.

· Track regional caseload metrics: volume, time-to-triage, time-to-resolution, and SLA adherence. Provide accurate regional data to the Global TAO Manager for program-wide reporting.

· Identify regional throughput issues or patterns — spikes in case type, emerging threat profiles, recurring escalation triggers — and raise them with analysis and proposed action.

· Establish and maintain partnerships with local stakeholders to assess Airbnb’s methodology of managing threatening incidents and to exchange threat information to reduce and minimize risks to the Airbnb community within the region.

· Manage regional Global Safety and Security team relationships with local law enforcement partners and other investigative, research, and intelligence groups and vendors.

Your Expertise

· 5+ years of experience in threat assessment, investigations, law enforcement, intelligence, or a closely related field.

· Hands-on threat assessment case experience: you have independently triaged, assessed, and managed cases involving targeted violence, stalking, harassment, or comparable subjects

· Solid documentation discipline: you write clear, accurate case notes that stand up to legal and operational scrutiny.

· Clear written and verbal communication: you can summarize a complex, sensitive case for a non-expert stakeholder and present a recommended action with confidence.

· Background in law enforcement, corporate security, intelligence, or a technology company trust and safety function with a case management component.

· Experience in a globally distributed team with cross-regional collaboration.

Mastery of open source research and online investigative techniques.

· Ability to build partnerships and work collaboratively and cross-functionally.

· Creative and entrepreneurial mindset with a positive attitude and hunger for learning.

· Willingness and ability to travel within the region as needed.

· Demonstrated commitment to Airbnb’s core values.

This position is US - Remote Eligible. The role may include occasional work at an Airbnb office or attendance at offsites, as agreed to with your manager. The Employee Experience team exists to help Airbnb become the company that it needs to be.
The Regional Workplace Operations Manager sits at the intersection of workplace experience, events, and gathering & culture. This role is responsible for bringing our brand to life by creating an intentional, welcoming, and high-functioning office experience that enables employees, leaders, and guests to feel connected, productive, and inspired.

Just like our hosts can offer differentiated experiences to our guests, our Regional Workplace Operations Manager exemplifies those aspirational expectations.
This role serves as the connective tissue across office operations, hospitality, employee engagement, and local community experience. They partner closely with cross-functional stakeholders including Talent, IT, Security, Communications, Executive Support, and local leaders to ensure each office reflects Airbnb’s culture and values in a meaningful and scalable way. They integrate platform hosts in the day to day office experience spotlighting service and experience hosts as appropriate.

As the Regional Workplace Operations Manager, you are the primary steward of the employee and guest experience within your office. You create a hospitality-forward environment where people feel welcomed, supported, and connected to Airbnb and each other.
You will oversee the daily office experience while also leading local gathering and engagement efforts that strengthen culture and community. You will direct and coordinate embedded vendors and operational partners to ensure seamless execution across hospitality, food, facilities, and events. You will provide oversight and mentorship to Office Managers within your region, ensuring consistency of standards and experience across proximate offices.
Success in this role requires strong operational ownership, exceptional interpersonal instincts, creativity, and the ability to navigate ambiguity while balancing both strategic thinking and hands-on execution.
You must have your finger on the pulse and anticipate the needs of each guest.

Lead Through Hospitality
Maintain a visible, approachable, and highly responsive presence within the office community.
Create a warm, thoughtful, and highly responsive environment where employees and visitors feel genuinely welcomed and cared for.
Lead with calmness, flexibility, and attention to detail while balancing multiple priorities and adapting to changing business needs.
Support and guide vendors and partners to operate as one cohesive hospitality team in service of the office community.
Drive Operational Excellence
Establish and maintain office operating standards that ensure consistency of hospitality, communication, service delivery, and workplace experience.
Monitor office utilization, employee feedback, operational performance, and service quality to identify opportunities for improvement.
Contribute local insights and best practices that help shape the evolution of workplace standards across the broader portfolio.
Develop repeatable processes and playbooks that enable scalable, high-quality office experiences.
Own the Office Experience
Oversee the holistic daily office experience, ensuring the space operates smoothly and delivers a welcoming, hospitality-forward environment for employees and guests.
You have a strong sense of ownership. Treat the office as your listing.
Serve as the day-to-day steward of the office environment, ensuring the space is operationally seamless, hospitality-forward, and consistently ready to support great work, connection, and high-visibility moments.
Provide operational oversight and direction to on-site vendors and service partners.
Direct and orchestrate on-site vendors and operational vendors including food, facilities, events, and hospitality to ensure consistent service delivery and experience quality. Own escalation management and drive resolution
Partner closely with Security, IT and other operational teams to ensure seamless day-to-day operations.
Act as the “Voice of the Office,” helping employees navigate the workplace experience and ensuring the office feels connected, informed, and supported.
Monitor employee sentiment and proactively identify opportunities to improve the office experience, communication, and engagement.
Enable Gathering & Engagement Experiences
Ensure the office is consistently prepared to support high-visibility visits, events, and business moments.
Partner with Regional Gathering Programs to support successful delivery of offsites, leadership visits and strategic gatherings.
Provide local stakeholder coordination, hospitality leadership, vendor management, and onsite execution support as needed.
Support onsite execution for local events, offsites, and engagement activities, ensuring thoughtful hospitality, operational excellence, and strong attendee experience.
Adapt office experiences to local needs while maintaining consistency with Airbnb culture and values.
Build Strong Partnerships
Develop strong relationships with local leaders, executive admins, Airfinity groups, cross-functional partners and other key stakeholders.
Act as a trusted partner and connector across teams, helping identify opportunities to strengthen office culture, engagement, and employee experience.
Partner with leaders to support meaningful moments of connection within the office and across teams.

6–9+ years of experience in workplace experience, hospitality, events, employee engagement, operations, or related fields
Experience owning and executing programs, events, or operational experiences end-to-end
Strong hospitality mindset with a passion for creating thoughtful and high-quality experiences
Experience managing vendors, operational partners, or service delivery teams
Strong stakeholder management and relationship-building skills across diverse teams and leadership levels
Ability to operate autonomously, navigate ambiguity, and manage multiple priorities simultaneously
Strong organizational and operational execution skills with attention to detail
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Experience supporting employee engagement, cultural programming, gatherings, or community-building initiatives is preferred
Ability to balance strategic thinking with hands-on execution
Passion for Airbnb’s mission, culture, and values
This role is expected to be based in-office full-time in our Seattle office, with flexibility for occasional evenings or weekends in support of events and gatherings.

About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

The Finance Operations (FinOps) team provides and enhances core business services that are the backbone of Stripe. FinOps uses data and operational excellence to deliver technology solutions, payroll services, operational excellence, and monetization services to Stripe.

We're looking for a Monetization Operations Analyst to join our growing team. You'll help us improve user experience through accurate and timely onboarding of contracts and workflows, and deliver improvements in our integrated financial systems with business partners, financial colleagues, and engineers.

The Stripe Delivery Center (SDC) strategy will provide operational leverage and expand Stripe’s portfolio of operational capabilities to support the scaled needs for external users and internal Stripe teams.

Stripe is launching Stripe Delivery Centers - a new global team to design, implement and grow Stripe’s operations for the next decade. In this role, you will recruit, manage, and develop a group of Operations Associates that are focused on user support. This person will cultivate the happiness of their team members while guiding them to be the best they can be, through feedback, coaching, mentoring, and advocacy within the organization.

This means helping to set team goals, and using metrics to efficiently measure and guide team performance in pursuit of those goals. To be a fit, you will have a strong operations mindset, be able to move quickly, and be passionate about delivering an incredible user experience.

About Gusto
At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.
All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .
AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

At Gusto, building a great product and delivering a great service aren't separate tracks — they have to move together, and that's what Service Transformation Product Operations exists to ensure.

As a Principal Product Operations Manager, you'll own some of the most cross-cutting work in the Customer Experience org: shaping how new products and features come to market, leading service design that identifies where AI can create the most leverage across the service experience, and operating as the connective tissue between Product, CX, Engineering, Legal, and GTM.

This is not a coordination role — you'll drive strategy, build and deploy AI-powered workflows, and bring rigor, creativity, and a bias toward execution to problems that don't yet have obvious answers.

The mission of our Service Transformation (ST) team is to evolve and scale how Gusto delivers outstanding service experiences — and to leverage AI to do it faster and better. We design the systems, processes, and feedback loops that let Gusto's product and service improve together, continuously and reliably, in a way that earns the trust of the small businesses we serve and the Gusto teams who serve them.
ST Product Operations is a cross-functional team sitting at the intersection of Product and CX — responsible not just for making today's experience better, but for shaping how new products and features come to market and how AI changes what great service looks like at scale. If something is broken, we fix it. If something needs to be built, we build it. If a new capability is ready to ship, we make sure it lands well.

Shape and drive strategy at the intersection of Gusto's Product and Service orgs — working closely with Engineering, Design, Product Management, and Customer Experience to improve existing products, launch net-new capabilities, and ensure the service experience scales alongside them.
Own the end-to-end CX strategy and implementation for net-new product and service launches — from determining how customers will be supported to engaging external partners — while ensuring every new capability meets Gusto's rigorous service standards before and after it goes live.
Lead strategic service design work alongside Product Management and CX teams — mapping end-to-end service blueprints, identifying where AI can augment or accelerate work done by service teams, and designing the handoffs and escalation logic that keep quality high as automation scales.
Build, deploy, and iterate on AI-powered workflows that improve how Gusto's service operations run — from automating intake and documentation to designing agentic systems that resolve customer needs faster and more reliably.
Serve as an AI thought leader within ST Product Operations — identify where AI can accelerate how the team works, set the bar for how those opportunities get acted on, and partner with teammates to propose, build, and adopt solutions that raise the baseline for everyone.
Provide business insights and recommendations grounded in quantitative and qualitative data to influence both product and service roadmaps. Communicate in a way that drives action — translating complex operational dynamics into clear direction for senior stakeholders.
Identify and lead cross-functional initiatives that deliver measurable value for customers and for Gusto — building the roadmap, aligning stakeholders, and seeing work through from framing to execution.

9+ years of relevant experience in product operations, service design, business operations, strategy, or program management — ideally at a company where you were building or improving a product and service simultaneously.
Demonstrated track record working at the cutting edge of AI implementation over the last two to three years — you've built agentic workflows, automated service or operational processes using AI tooling, or designed AI-assisted systems in production. You're not learning to do this; you've done it.
Experience with service design or service blueprinting — you understand how to map a customer journey end-to-end, identify failure points, and design systems that hold up at scale.
Proven ability to own and improve complex, cross-functional launch or release processes — you know what it takes to bring a product to market well and have built the coordination systems to make it repeatable.
Strong results-orientation with the ability to extract and interpret data to identify trends and influence decisions — comfortable doing this with or without AI assistance, and fluent in knowing which approach fits the moment.
Experienced at influencing senior stakeholders across Product, Engineering, CX, Legal, and Compliance — in writing, in design reviews, and in high-stakes forums.
Experience leading through change — whether guiding a team, driving an organizational transformation, or helping others adapt to new systems and ways of working.
Highly adaptable and able to create structure in ambiguous environments. You've built the plane while flying it before, and that energizes rather than exhausts you.
Deep empathy for small business customers and a genuine obsession with making their experience better.
Our cash compensation amount for this role is $148,085/yr to $182,638/yr in Denver & most major metro locations, and $167,345/yr to $217,549/yr for San Francisco & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

Commissions are one of the most consequential things Revenue Operations owns. Every month and every quarter, the entire go-to-market organization is paid based on numbers we run — and the person who gets them right, on time, and clearly explained earns the trust of the whole field.
We're looking for a Revenue Operations Manager to own that process end to end. This is a hands-on, individual-contributor role with real ownership from day one.

You'll run the full commissions payout cycle — monthly and quarterly — administer our commissions platform, safeguard the data behind every payout, and be the go-to for anyone with a question about how they were paid.

And because you'll own the whole process, you'll have the room to improve it: you'll look for ways to make it faster and cleaner, and you'll use AI to take the repetitive work off your plate, so your time goes to the parts that need real judgment. If you like the idea of taking something important and making it run well, this role is for you.
This role will be located out of our Seattle / Bellevue office, working closely with the team in New York and stakeholders in other international locations.

Own the commissions payout cycle. Run calculation, validation, approvals, and on-time payout for both the monthly and quarterly cycles, end to end, in partnership with Finance and Payroll.
Master CaptivateIQ. Be the owner and administrator of our ICM platform — configuring and maintaining plans, rules, rates, and data feeds, and keeping it the single source of truth for everything commissions-related.
Safeguard data integrity. Reconcile inputs across Salesforce, Looker, BambooHR, and CaptivateIQ so every payout is accurate, traceable, and audit-ready. When the numbers don't tie out, you find out why.
Be the go-to for the field. Handle commission inquiries, disputes, and adjustments with clarity and speed, and help reps and managers understand exactly how they're paid.
Continuously improve the process. Treat "the way it's always been done" as a starting point, not an answer. Constantly look for ways to make the cycle faster, cleaner, and less manual.
Put AI to work. Use AI to automate the lower-value, repetitive parts of the job — data prep, reconciliation, routine inquiry handling — so the time you spend is on analysis and judgment, not copy-paste.
Support comp plan rollout. Partner with RevOps and Finance on plan design, modeling, and clean implementation each planning cycle.
Report on commissions. Give leadership clear, trustworthy visibility into commission spend and attainment.

3+ years in sales compensation / commissions administration, sales/GTM operations, RevOps, or FP&A — ideally in a fast-paced B2B SaaS environment.

Hands-on mastery of CaptivateIQ (or a comparable ICM tool, such as Qobra), including plan configuration and day-to-day administration.

Strong analytical and spreadsheet skills; comfortable working with large data sets, CRM and BI tool data (Salesforce & Looker).

Exceptional accuracy and attention to detail, with a track record of hitting payout deadlines without exception.

A genuine process-improvement instinct — you're never quite satisfied with the current state and you enjoy making things run better.

Real fluency with AI tools and a habit of reaching for them to automate repetitive work.

Clear written and verbal communication, and the judgment to handle sensitive compensation conversations discreetly.

Docker has been one of the most loved brands in developer tooling, trusted by more than 20 million monthly users and over 20 billion container image pulls. From solo founders to the world's largest companies, developers rely on Docker to build, share, and run their applications across our suite of products including Docker Desktop, Docker Hub, and Docker Scout.
We are a globally distributed, remote-first team building the tools that define how software gets built and delivered. As AI agents redefine software development, Docker is at the center of that shift, providing the sandboxed environments, verified images, and secure infrastructure that make autonomous workflows trustworthy by default.
Docker’s event portfolio - flagship conferences, developer roadshows, digital events, and community activations - is how Docker shows up in the world and turns developer enthusiasm into enterprise pipeline. As the portfolio grows, operational excellence is what lets it scale without added risk or complexity.
As a Senior Event Operations Manager , you will own the operational execution of that portfolio. Working closely with Docker's Director of Events, you coordinate planning timelines, manage vendors and logistics, own budgets and the event tech stack, and build the repeatable playbooks that keep programs running smoothly and consistently across the year.
This role is ideal for someone who enjoys building systems, bringing structure to fast-moving projects, and delivering high-quality experiences at scale.
You will report to the Director of Events within Marketing and partner daily with Product Marketing, Developer Relations, Field Marketing, and Sales.
Please note: for this role, you must have the ability to travel 35% of the time across North America, along with international travel as-needed.
What Success Looks Like
Success in this role is operational: events are delivered smoothly and consistently across the portfolio, teams have clear planning processes and execution frameworks to work from, and operational risks are identified early and resolved quickly. Above all, programs are able to grow and scale without increasing complexity, because the systems, playbooks, and budgets you build absorb that growth.

Own operational execution across the event portfolio - major conferences, developer roadshows, digital events, and community activations - managing timelines, project plans, and execution milestones across multiple concurrent events, and keeping them on schedule, on budget, and aligned to internal goals.
Maintain a master event calendar that coordinates timing, resourcing, and dependencies across programs.
Manage event registration, attendee experience, and lead capture and badging across the portfolio.
Build scalable event operations: repeatable planning templates, run-of-show frameworks, and operational playbooks, continuously simplifying and improving execution over time.
Own the event technology stack (registration, mobile apps, lead retrieval) and ensure data flows cleanly into marketing and sales systems.
Manage vendors and logistics: agencies, venues, production vendors, and internal teams, including contract execution, budget tracking, shipping, production schedules, and onsite readiness.
Own end-to-end event budgets, including purchase orders, invoicing, and post-event reconciliation.
Partner cross-functionally with Marketing, Product Marketing, Developer Relations, Field Marketing, and Sales, translating program goals into clear operational plans.
Operationalize developer-focused programs - roadshows, community activations, and flagship conference experiences - and build frameworks that let them expand to additional markets over time.
Track event KPIs and pipeline/ROI, run post-event debriefs, and lead reconciliation and timely handoff to sales.
Provide operational and logistics support to Field Marketing across regional events, roadshows, and third-party/sponsored events, including sponsorship deliverables, booth and presence logistics, and lead retrieval.

6+ years in full-time, professional event management, event operations, and/or experiential program management.
Strong project management skills, with a track record coordinating complex programs across multiple stakeholders and concurrent events without losing attention to detail.
Must have the ability to travel 35% of the time across North America, with potential for international travel
Hands-on vendor, agency, and production-partner management, including contracts, budgets, and performance.
Comfortable using AI to scale repeatable processes without sacrificing quality.
Demonstrated professional experience with event and marketing tech (registration platforms, lead retrieval, mobile apps) and how event data flows into Salesforce and Marketo and lead management workflows.
Experience building operational frameworks or playbooks that let event programs scale.
Developer, technical, or enterprise event experience is highly preferred; background in SaaS, developer platforms, cloud, or technology companies is an advantage.
Comfort working in fast-moving environments where priorities can evolve.
What to Expect
First 30 Days
Immerse in Docker’s event portfolio, the master calendar, the event tech stack, and current vendor and agency relationships.
Audit live programs and operational processes; identify where timelines, budgets, and handoffs carry the most risk.
Build working relationships with the Director of Events, Field Marketing, Product Marketing, Developer Relations, and Sales.
Take ownership of operational execution for the next event on the calendar.
First 90 Days
Stand up or refine repeatable planning templates, run-of-show frameworks, and operational playbooks across the portfolio.
Establish a master event calendar that coordinates timing, resourcing, and dependencies.
Deliver a flagship event or roadshow end to end, on schedule and on budget, with clean lead capture and sales handoff.
Establish a post-event debrief and KPI/ROI reporting cadence that informs future planning and investment.
One-Year Outlook
Run an event operations function that scales with the portfolio without adding risk or complexity.
Own end-to-end budgets and vendor relationships with reliable reconciliation and reporting.
Expand developer-focused programs to additional markets on repeatable frameworks.
Be the operational backbone the events and field marketing teams rely on for consistent, high-quality execution.

We are looking for a Revenue Operations Analyst to improve how we use data across marketing, sales, customer success, product, and billing.
Your main responsibility is to understand how our revenue processes perform and why results change. You will define metrics, combine data from different systems, investigate patterns, and test assumptions.
Your analyses should lead to measurable improvements. This may involve a better decision, a change to an existing process, or an automation that removes manual work and improves reliability.
Reporting and dashboards are part of the role, but they are not the objective. Each analysis should answer a relevant business question and provide a clear basis for the next decision.
You will also implement selected solutions, including data models, dashboards, and automations. Analysis remains the main focus. Implementation follows when the expected impact and method of measurement are clear.
Previous professional experience is useful but not required. We value analytical judgement, accuracy, technical understanding, and the ability to learn.
Tasks
Analyse the customer journey from acquisition and conversion to retention and revenue.
Define and maintain consistent metrics across marketing, sales, customer success, product, and finance.
Extract, combine, clean, and validate data from operational and analytical systems.
Investigate changes in customer behaviour, funnels, conversion rates, retention, costs, and revenue.
Determine the likely causes of performance changes instead of only describing the result.
Review existing reports and identify unreliable metrics, missing data, and conflicting definitions.
Develop hypotheses and test them against the available data.
Distinguish evidence from assumptions, correlations, and opinions.
Estimate the expected impact of proposed changes and define how success will be measured.
Prioritise opportunities based on impact, effort, and the reliability of the supporting data.
Present findings and recommendations in a form that supports business decisions.
Build selected dashboards, data models, automations, and process improvements.
Measure implemented changes and assess whether they produced the expected result.
Use AI assistants as a daily tool for research, data exploration, coding support, and documentation.
Verify AI-generated results against the underlying data and original sources.
Document metric definitions, data logic, assumptions, methods, and limitations.

Strong analytical skills and a structured approach to solving problems.
A high standard for data quality and reliable results.
General programming knowledge and an interest in developing your technical skills.
Initial experience with SQL, Python, JavaScript, APIs, spreadsheets, data warehouses, or business intelligence tools is beneficial.
A basic understanding of statistics, including the difference between correlation and causation.
The ability to examine a problem from different perspectives before reaching a conclusion.
Interest in using AI assistants as part of analytical and technical work.
The judgement to review AI-generated results critically.
The ability to explain complex findings in clear language.
The motivation to learn unfamiliar tools, systems, and business areas.
The discipline to follow an analysis until the result is sufficiently reliable.
You’ll always know what’s expected of you, and you’ll work in an environment where mistakes are seen as valuable opportunities to learn.

s.h: How you’ll plan your day (and life)
s.t:
We work async at Remote which means you can plan your schedule around your life (and not around meetings). Read more at remote.com/async .
You will be empowered to take ownership and be proactive. When in doubt you will default to action instead of waiting. Your life-work balance is important and you will be encouraged to put yourself and your family first, and fit work around your needs.
If that sounds like something you want, apply now!

About Remote
Remote is solving modern organizations’ biggest challenge – navigating global employment compliantly with ease. We make it possible for businesses of all sizes to recruit, pay, and manage international teams. With our core values at heart and future focused work culture, our team works tirelessly on ambitious problems, asynchronously, around the world. You can find Remoters working from 6 different continents (Antarctica left to go!) and all of our positions are fully remote.
With Innovation as one of the core values, we have built Automation and AI capabilities into the requirements for every role.
We encourage every member of the Remote team to bring their talents, experiences and culture to the table to help us build the best-in-class HR platform.
If you are energetic, curious, motivated and ambitious, be part of our world. Apply now and define the future of work!
What this job can offer you
In this role, you’ll shape Remote’s most critical revenue growth decisions by operating at the intersection of strategy, analytics, and execution.
You’ll lead high-impact, data-driven initiatives that influence executive-level priorities and overall business direction. This role combines analytical rigor, business acumen, and senior stakeholder management to solve complex commercial challenges.
You’ll gain exposure to C-level decision-making, take end-to-end ownership of strategic initiatives, and see your recommendations drive measurable business outcomes in a fast-paced, global environment.
Team members are aligned to one or more GTM leaders and act as strategic business partners helping solve complex business challenges, identify growth opportunities, and drive execution of key initiatives. Depending on business needs and candidate strengths, this role may support leaders across Marketing, Sales, or Partnerships.

Outstanding analytical and structured problem-solving skills
Extensive experience in a top-tier strategy consulting firm, or in a strategic role within a high-growth startup or scale-up (e.g. strategy, business operations, corporate development, growth)
Ability to generate insights from data and connect them to actionable strategic recommendations
Strong leadership and ownership skills, and the ability to work autonomously while linking back to overall business strategy
Experience leading complex initiatives end-to-end, from hypothesis generation to solution implementation
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English, including the ability to influence senior stakeholders
Intellectual curiosity, critical thinking, and a bias for action
Collaborative mindset and adaptability in a fast-changing environment
Comfort with ambiguity and a willingness to dive deep into unstructured business problems
Passion for technology and understanding of trends and market dynamics in SaaS and B2B software markets
Great senior stakeholder management skills
Demonstrates strong automation and AI capabilities and AI fluency.

Explicit Strategic Business Partnering: Serve as a dedicated strategic business partner to one or more GTM leaders, helping identify opportunities, solve business challenges, and drive execution against strategic priorities.
Commercialization: Partner with Product, PMM, Pricing, and Enablement teams to assess commercial readiness and support the successful commercialization of new products, capabilities, and strategic initiatives.
Revenue Performance & Opportunity Analysis: Analyze revenue performance and customer behavior to identify opportunities for growth, efficiency, and improved commercial outcomes.
Identify and frame high-impact business problems related to revenue growth using a mix of data analysis, market insights, and stakeholder input
Conduct structured quantitative and qualitative analysis to uncover opportunities and assess trade-offs
Synthesize complex findings into clear, actionable strategies and communicate them to C-level audiences
Influence senior stakeholders to gain buy-in for strategic recommendations and drive execution across the organisation
Lead cross-functional strategic initiatives end-to-end, from problem definition to alignment, execution, and performance measurement
Build trusted relationships with cross-functional leaders and executives to proactively surface and shape high-priority initiatives
Act as a generalist thought partner to revenue leaders, helping them solve complex business challenges
Practicals
You'll report to: Head of GTM Strategy
Team: GTM Strategy
Location : For this position we welcome everyone to apply, but we will prioritize applications from the following locations as we encourage our teams to diversify: EMEA and Americas
Start date: As soon as possible
Application process
Roughly 4 hours across 4 weeks
Interview with recruiter
Interview with Head of GTM Strategy
Take home case study
Case study presentation with SVP, Revenue, Strategy & RevOps + Head of GTM Strategy
Interview with either VP, Growth Marketing or General Manager, Partnership Business
Bar raiser interview
Prior employment verification check
Remote's Total Rewards philosophy is to ensure fair, unbiased compensation and fair equity pay along with competitive benefits in all locations in which we operate. We do not agree to or encourage cheap-labor practices and therefore we ensure to pay above in-location rates. We hope to inspire other companies to support global talent-hiring and bring local wealth to developing countries.
At first glance our salary bands seem quite wide - here is some context. At Remote we have international operations and a globally distributed workforce. We use geo ranges to consider geographic pay differentials as part of our global compensation strategy to remain competitive in various markets while we hiring globally.
Our salary ranges are determined by role, level and location, and our job titles may span more than one career level. The actual base pay for the successful candidate in this role is dependent upon many factors such as location, transferable or job-related skills, work experience, relevant training, business needs, and market demands. The base salary range may be subject to change.
At Remote, we foster internal mobility as a key element of our culture of employee growth and development, supported by a compensation philosophy that guarantees pay equity and fairness. Therefore, all compensation changes associated with an internal move will be reviewed by the Total Rewards & People Enablement team on a case by case basis.

Our full benefits & perks are explained in our handbook at remote.com/r/benefits . As a global company, each country works differently, but some benefits/perks are for all Remoters:
work from anywhere
flexible paid time off
flexible working hours (we are async )
16 weeks paid parental leave
mental health support services
stock options
learning budget
home office budget & IT equipment
budget for local in-person social events or co-working spaces

GitLab is looking for a Hyperscaler Operations Manager to join our Ecosystem Operations team. This role combines deep operational governance across GitLab's AWS and GCP partnerships with the successful execution of hyperscaler operational initiatives, serving as the operational architect of the hyperscaler GTM and the primary process owner for marketplace, co-sell, and funding operations.
You will own the technology, processes, and operational infrastructure that underpin GitLab's hyperscaler motions, serving as the go-to resource for hyperscaler partners and internal teams. This role sits at the intersection of cloud marketplace mechanics, hyperscaler funding, and systems administration, requiring someone equally comfortable setting GTM strategy, executing operationally, and leveraging AI to automate and scale hyperscaler processes.
You will work closely with Systems, Revenue Technologies, Deal Desk, Enablement, Finance, and Legal to ensure GitLab's hyperscaler operations are accurate, scalable, and aligned to partnership objectives.

Marketplace Operational Strategy & Execution
Establish, oversee, and continuously improve end-to-end marketplace operational processes, including private offer management, CPPO/MCPO structures, and third-party integrations
Serve as the internal expert on the private offer process end-to-end, partnering closely with Deal Desk to define, document, and iterate on workflows across AWS and GCP
Own operational execution of hyperscaler funding initiatives such as AWS Strategic Collaboration Agreement (SCA), Marketplace Private Offer Partner Program (MPOPP), and GCP Marketplace Commit to Consume Program (MCCP), including milestone tracking, deal registration, claim workflows, and commit management
Serve as the escalation point for marketplace and funding operations, resolving complex private offer, co-sell, and billing issues that span multiple systems or stakeholders
Technology Ownership & Administration
Serve as the primary relationship owner for the hyperscaler technology ecosystem, including Salesforce CRM partner objects, Tackle.io, and hyperscaler-specific PRM configurations
Administer hyperscaler platforms, maintaining system health and data integrity across all hyperscaler-specific tools and integrations
Co-manage vendor relationships, including Tackle.io and other marketplace tooling providers, covering roadmap engagement, renewal coordination, and SLA accountability
Identify and build AI agents to automate repetitive hyperscaler workflows, such as offer status tracking, reporting, and co-sell registration, reducing manual effort and increasing operational throughput
Partner with RevTech and Systems to maintain integration health across hyperscaler platforms, CRM, and downstream financial systems, including funding success tracking and reporting
Hyperscaler Funding Initiatives & Operational Management
Drive the operational strategy for hyperscaler funding initiatives across AWS and GCP, translating partnership objectives into co-sell and marketplace revenue plays
Serve as the point of contact for hyperscaler partners and internal sales teams on funding operations, co-sell execution, utilization, and cross-functional escalations
Identify opportunities to align hyperscaler funding with pipeline priorities and revenue goals
Monitor funding performance across marketplace revenue, co-sell pipeline, and utilization; coordinate with Finance, AR, and Legal on billing and commitments
Process Design, Governance & Enablement
Design, document, and govern end-to-end hyperscaler operational processes, including marketplace, co-sell, and funding initiatives, owning and maintaining the hyperscaler process map as the authoritative reference
Continuously evaluate hyperscaler processes for AI automation opportunities, building and deploying agents that improve consistency, reduce cycle time, and scale operational capacity
Drive gap remediation through cross-functional engagement with RSO peers and adjacent teams in IT, Finance, and Legal
Build and maintain operational runbooks, process documentation, and training materials enabling consistent execution across all cross-functional partners
Support configuration, testing, and maintenance of hyperscaler-facing and internal tools; document workflows and lead end-user training for field and operational teams
Lead prioritization for hyperscaler system implementations, migrations, and platform enhancements with IT/Enterprise Applications
Proactively surface process improvement opportunities and create GitLab Issues to advance the enhancement kickoff process

6+ years of experience in cloud marketplace operations with direct ownership of hyperscaler-related workflows
Hands-on experience with Tackle.io or equivalent cloud marketplace management platforms (AWS and GCP Marketplaces)
Working knowledge of Salesforce CRM, including partner objects, opportunity management, and basic administration
Deep familiarity with AWS and GCP marketplace mechanics, including private offer creation, CPPO/MCPO structures, co-sell registration, and billing and disbursement workflows
Direct experience managing hyperscaler funding initiatives such as SCA, MPOPP, and MCCP, including strategy, operational execution, and compliance requirements
Familiarity with hyperscaler co-sell operations, including AWS ACE and GCP Partner Advantage structures and operational requirements
Demonstrated ability to design and document complex operational processes enabling consistent execution across distributed teams
Hands-on experience working with AI tools and building agents to automate operational workflows; comfort evaluating processes for automation potential and translating them into working solutions

We are looking for a detail-oriented and customer-focused professional to join our Billing team. You will work closely with customers to provide precise and timely invoices while also collaborate with different teams to ensure a smooth billing process end to end.
In this role, you will become an integral part of our team, supporting the essential functions of billing operations and contributing to the overall efficiency of our processes. We're looking for someone who is detail-oriented and enjoys working with numbers, as you'll manage billing data and help ensure accuracy across various platforms. If you're ready to take on a position that allows you to develop your skills in a cooperative environment, we would love to hear from you.
What You Will Be Doing
Verify the accuracy of sales orders prior to processing invoices.
Address any discrepancies with customers and coordinate with other departments to address billing issues.
Upload invoices into various portals to ensure proficient operations.
Test automation tools to improve and streamline billing operations.
Collaborate with team members to design and implement process enhancements that boost efficiency.
Manage billing case inquiries and actively track their resolution progress. Analyze case data to identify patterns and recommend improvements.
Collaborate with internal teams to address any questions and document case details to maintain correct records for reporting.
Keeping internal documents up to date and maintenance of internal SOP's

Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, or a related field
2+ years with billing operations and invoice processing systems
SFDC and NetSuite experience is a plus
Proficiency in MS Excel or Google Spreadsheet- VLOOKUP, pivot tables, analysis
Accustomed to working with case management system
Experience with customer billing dispute resolution
Ability to co-ordinate with cross-functional teams to optimize process workflows
Proficient communication skills, both verbal and written and attention to detail
Creative problem solving skills
Capacity to work autonomously and prioritize in distributed, dynamic environment

We are seeking an exceptional Sales Ops Professional (Individual Contributor) to help drive sales strategy, planning, reporting, and analysis efforts for our APJ business covering India and Japan markets. The Revenue Strategy & Operations Manager will be responsible for the analytical aspects of key business decisions, including go-to-market strategies, resource allocation, process improvement, metrics and dashboards.
You must be able to work cross-functionally to drive efficiency and performance improvement across multiple operational and financial metrics throughout APJ. You will generate reports and analysis, providing insights that support decision-making and help define, land, and execute on our key strategic priorities for the geography.
You will support running the business cadence, helping navigate the complexities of systems and tools as well as collaborating with cross-functional teams to solve problems, design, manage, and successfully deliver projects against operational standards.
The Revenue Strategy & Operations Manager will help scale the operations of Elastic’s APJ business by providing the systems and business insights the organization needs to optimize sales performance, effectiveness and productivity.

Responsibilities will include pipeline analysis, sales performance analyses, forecast preparation, territory management, quota assignment, report preparation and deep analysis of our efficiency in the market.

The Revenue Strategy & Operations Manager enjoys analyzing data, loves disrupting the inefficient, and is not afraid to "get their hands dirty". This person will be results-oriented, flexible, and eager to acquire new skills and knowledge.
What You Will Be Doing
Partner closely with sales leadership to develop actionable, measurable projects and programs that accelerate sales growth and improve sales rep productivity.
Perform in-depth analyses on the leading, in-process, and lagging indicators to support strategic initiatives to drive growth.
Provide analytical and day-to-day operational activities support.
Perform data analysis and modeling to identify trends and efficiency opportunities. Build and maintain tools and dashboards to help with reporting and analytical needs of the team and key stakeholders.
Engage in ad-hoc analyses to understand business performance/user metrics, Key Performance Indicators and provide concise summaries and recommendations to management.
Identify process gaps and opportunities for process improvement.
Provide analytical insights into aspects of key business decisions, including go-to-market strategies, resource allocation, process improvement, metrics and dashboards
Detailed analysis of the pipeline and insights to grow pipeline generation efforts and conversion rates.
Identify levers for driving revenue growth and sales efficiency.
Conduct detailed analysis of sales productivity.
Support sales forecasting and annual planning processes.
Provide system and tool support to the field to enhance sales productivity.
Manage and facilitate regular business reviews with sales and cross-functional leadership
Focus on continuous improvement of sales processes and tools to drive productivity and remove friction

BS/BA or equivalent required
5+ years work experience in Sales, Sales Operations, Strategy, FP&A, Management Consulting, or similar field in SaaS organizations with strong exposure to go-to-market strategy.
Demonstrated ability to structure complex problems, develop solutions, and craft recommendations and results into easily digestible messages, communications, and executive presentations.
Excellent communication and engagement skills.
Highly collaborative style and the ability to adjust on the fly to new demands with a sense of urgency.
Ability to thrive in a fast paced start-up environment.
Experience with the Salesforce.com platform
Experience with Microsoft Office Suite.

Proficiency in Japanese Language is a plus.

As Procurement Operations Manager, your primary focus will be to architect and manage the systems, processes, and analytical frameworks that empower the global sourcing and procurement organization.

You will be reporting to the Senior Manager, Strategic Sourcing in North America, to transform procurement operations into a data-driven engine of efficiency.

You will work closely with global sourcing leads to drive value through operational excellence, automation, and high-quality organizational metrics across all technical and non-technical spend categories.

This role is highly cross-functional and requires consistent liaison with IT, Accounts Payable, and other key departments across the company to ensure operational alignment.
What You Will Be Doing
Operations, Systems, & Analytics

s.h: You will work with the Sourcing Leader to
s.t:
Act as project manager for the Sourcing team, keeping key projects on track and supporting weekly key deals reviews.
Improve procurement and contract management policies, processes, and procedures while ensuring compliance.
Develop and track key metrics including contract review cycle time, savings, supplier consolidation and relationship management, risk reduction and management, and improved visibility and control of expenditures.
Strengthen reporting and analytics across procurement and contract activities to highlight trends, risks, challenges, and opportunities.
Support implementation of systems and tools that drive productivity gains across procurement, sourcing, and contract management.
Serve as subject matter expert for procurement tools such as Workday, Lucid, BigQuery, Tableau, Netsuite, and Omnea, ensuring system integrity.
Support new procurement tool implementation through cross-functional collaboration and representation of sourcing interests.
Build and maintain advanced analytics dashboards for real-time visibility into global spend, contract cycle times, and supplier performance.
Architect and automate intake-to-pay workflows to remove manual bottlenecks and improve stakeholder experience.
Operational Support & Procurement Enablement

s.h: You and your team will be
s.t:
Overseeing the contract administration lifecycle and coordinating review processes using established playbooks to ensure compliance.
Managing tactical, high-volume procurement proposals and bids aligned with broader category strategies and technical requirements.
Operationalizing global agreements by partnering with Legal and IT to streamline execution of SOWs, MSAs, and NDAs.
Owning the training curriculum for the sourcing and procurement team to support development and knowledge sharing.
Rolling out automation projects to improve operations and efficiencies within the Sourcing team.

Expertise in procurement tools and systems implementation, including Workday, ServiceNow, Tableau, Lucid, Netsuite, Omnea, and similar platforms.
Strong analytics and reporting skills, with the ability to draw insights from complex data and improve procurement visibility.
Experience automating procurement workflows and intake-to-pay processes to drive productivity gains.
A Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in business, law, or equivalent, plus 7 to 10 years of relevant experience in sourcing and procurement operations.
Deep understanding of vendor contracts, purchasing, and contract review processes, with a focus on compliance and efficiency.
Experience leading international procurement operations and contract teams in global high-growth technology companies.
Ability to translate complex contractual terms into operational workflows and playbooks in partnership with Legal teams.
Strong leadership , coaching, presentation, and relationship-building skills, with the ability to manage a distributed team and influence business partners.
Ability to build strong relationships with key business partners and vendors, and lead purchasing projects across categories.
Flexibility to support global time zones, especially North America, and willingness to travel as needed.
A self-starter mindset with a positive, can-do attitude, initiative , and focus on results.
Passion for operational improvement, productivity gains, and performance metrics.
Proven ability to govern and orchestrate AI agents for tail spend management and contract intelligence, while helping upskill the procurement team for the AI era.
Active participation in procurement networks and industry forums such as SIG, with strong knowledge of AI-driven procurement tools, automation, and emerging trends.

As the Vice President of Asana Services Management & Incubation GTM, you’ll own Product Management, GTM strategy, and the incubation Sales Engineering / Forward Deployed team for Asana Service Management, Asana’s most promising 0→1 product.

Asana Service Management unifies ticketing and project execution for IT, HR, facilities, and other service teams to resolve key issues without human touch. This is a rare role with a direct reporting line across both Product Management and Sales Engineering / Forward-Deployed Engineering, combined with full P&L responsibility.
In this high-leverage VP-level role, you will act as an entrepreneurial leader.

You will sit at the intersection of sales, technical execution, and product development—owning the GTM strategy, engaging directly with mid-market customers to close business, and translating front-line market insights into a concrete product roadmap and product execution.

This is a "player-coach" role designed for someone who thrives in ambiguity and knows how to scale a technical GTM motion within a fast-growing SaaS environment.
This role is based in our San Francisco office with an office-centric hybrid schedule. The standard in-office days are Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday. Most Asanas have the option to work from home on Wednesdays. Working from home on Fridays depends on the type of work you do and the teams with which you partner. If you're interviewing for this role, your recruiter will share more about the in-office requirements.
What you’ll achieve
Drive Incubation GTM Strategy: Architect and execute the global commercial and go-to-market strategy for Asana for Service Management, taking it from early-stage concepts to repeatable, revenue-generating engines.
Engage with Customers & Assist in Closing Deals: Serve as a key executive sponsor and technical seller on strategic deals, regularly interfacing with enterprise customers to understand their complex workflows and build trust.
Own Product Roadmap and Product Execution: Act as the strategic voice of the market; synthesize deep customer feedback, competitor gaps, and field insights to define, prioritize and execute on the product roadmap.
Foster Cross-Functional Alignment: Bridge the gap internally between Sales, Product, Engineering, and Customer Success to ensure seamless execution of the services growth strategy.
Establish Metrics and Guardrails: Define, monitor, and optimize key performance indicators (KPIs) for the SE/FDE teams, incubation sales velocity, and partner services attach rates.

Demonstrates curiosity about AI tools and emerging technologies, with a willingness to learn and leverage them to enhance productivity, collaboration, or decision-making.
Proven GTM Leadership: 12+ years of experience in a Senior Director or VP-level capacity leading technical GTM, Product Management and/or Solutions Engineering within a prominent B2B SaaS environment (ideally within the ITSM, ESM spaces).
The "Startup" Mindset: A highly entrepreneurial, proactive builder who is comfortable operating with ambiguity and possesses a strong "player-coach" mentality—willing to roll up your sleeves to map out a technical architecture or pitch to a CIO.
Deep Technical Credibility: Strong background managing highly technical field resources (SEs, FDEs, or Solutions Architects) and a deep understanding of enterprise integrations, APIs, and SaaS architecture.
Market-Driven Product Vision: While formal Product Management (PM) experience is optional but preferred, you have a proven track record of translating complex customer and market needs into structured, actionable product requirements and priorities.
Commercial & Strategic Muscle Selling into IT Buyers: Demonstrated success selling to the IT buyer, managing a business unit's P&L, and designing scalable GTM frameworks.
Masterful Communicator: Exceptional ability to distill highly technical concepts into clear, value-driven narratives for executive stakeholders, cross-functional partners, and customers alike.
At Asana, we're committed to building teams that include a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills, as this is critical to helping us achieve our mission. If you're interested in this role and don't meet every listed requirement, we still encourage you to apply.
What we’ll offer

Monumental is automating on-site construction with robotics and software. Our mission is to make construction software-defined and autonomous - a future where beautiful, bespoke buildings go up in a single day, with minimal labour.
We're a growing team of engineers, operators and technicians from companies like Palantir, Qualcomm, Dyson, Shopify, Tesla, Meta and Google DeepMind. It's still the early days of building the company, and this is a chance to make an outsized impact on a problem that matters. From day one, you’ll be working with an experienced founding team backed, backed by a $32M Series B led by Khosla Ventures and Plural.
You'll be part of our founding US team - pilots are on the way as we expand into the market, with facilities to follow. To get you started, we'll cover travel and accommodation for a few weeks of onboarding at Monumental HQ, in the city centre of Amsterdam - a beautiful facility with an in-house workshop and robot testing floor. We're explicitly not a hybrid or remote-first company - you can't build robots or walls from home, so we're onsite five days a week.
Read more on why we believe you should spend your time working on construction, and learn about our vision and company . You might enjoy Based in Europe’s film on how we’re fixing Europe’s housing shortage , or this video by Andreas Klinger of what our office looks like .

We're looking for an extremely entrepreneurial operator. You’re going to be our first General Manager outside of Europe, so this is not going to be a role where you’ll follow some playbook to establish a new market: you’re going to figure out and write the playbook yourself, the hard and complicated way.
Monumental is unique in that we're completely vertically-integrated. We design and build our own hardware and software, we manufacture the robots in-house, and we deploy them on construction sites ourselves, with our own team, operating as a subcontractor.
If the prospect of deploying cutting-edge technology in an operationally complex environment that hasn't seen change for over a century, while doing sales and building up a local team doesn't daunt you, then you should definitely read on and apply.
You'll have an extraordinary amount of autonomy. It's an excellent fit if you've founded a company before, or if you're looking for an entrepreneurial role where you can make outsized impact. You'll get high level goals (see below) but no one will tell you what to do or manage you on a daily basis.
We are unable to support relocation or sponsorship for this role. Applicants must be based in the US, eligible to work willing for frequent travel between the US and the Netherlands.

Figure out how to go from small construction pilot deployments to ongoing commercial deployments, and then scale to multiple concurrent deployments. We expect you to act as the initial Deployment Manager in the US so you can build up enough tacit knowledge before scaling up.
Ensure there is always more than sufficient demand for our product. Our sales tends to be low-lift work, but you should still be excellent at it and always have the feeling that you're short on supply to meet the demand you've generated.
Hire, onboard, and manage a local team of robot and deployment operators that will operate our robots and other tasks on construction sites. We're planning to seed the US team with members from our Dutch team so you can hit the ground running and more easily bootstrap Monumental's unique culture in a new location.
Manage our fleet of robots and, with the rest of the HQ team, figure out how to manage a remote fleet across the Atlantic.
Set up whatever local facilities will be needed in the US, from a small office to a potential storage or maintenance hub.
Stand up the required legal structure for us to operate and scale in the US. This includes setting up local entities, navigating state and federal employment law, and all other relevant regulation. You're comfortable navigating complicated questions that involve new technology in old industries, liaising with the right counsel when needed.

Minimum of 6 years of experience in a chaotic, entrepreneurial, high-growth, unstructured environment. This could be as a startup founder, GM, sales, operations, business development or a similar area where you've seen rapid growth, and where we don't need to explain to you why grit and resilience are important character traits for this role.
A strong bias-to-action and getting-shit-done mentality with the required tenacity and speed. The emphasis of this role is execution, not making decks.
You're able to context switch from strategic work to very practical work throughout the day, and nothing feels beneath you. There will be days where in the morning you're literally getting your feet dirty, helping carry mortar on a construction site, while interviewing senior candidates in the afternoon.
A strong strategic business sense. You have proven experience doing sales, pricing, negotiations, and account management. You're comfortable being responsible for the P&L of your deployments and the entire US operation.
You're an excellent communicator. You need to be comfortable chatting with people from all over the construction industry, from billionaire real estate developers to junior tradesmen on the construction site.
You have experience hiring and managing a team and you understand the importance of filtering for and instilling the right culture. You'll be responsible for hiring the initial team in the US.
Raw intellectual horsepower and eagerness to learn. We expect this role to have a steep learning curve whatever your background, and this role might in practice feel like a completely new job every 3-6 months.
Willingness for frequent travel within the US, and between the US & The Netherlands. We expect you to spend a significant amount of time in The Netherlands in the first 3-6 months for onboarding and immersion, and then likely some travel cadence after.
A child-like excitement and optimism to be building the future, with robots, that will build houses for people to live in.
Why Monumental?
Joining Monumental means being at the forefront of a movement aimed at making significant strides in the construction industry. Here, your work has the potential to impact not just the company but the future of how we build. If you're driven by innovation, eager to tackle complex challenges, and ready to make a tangible difference, we want to hear from you.

A day in the life: The AI Operations Manager is the operating system behind the Innovation team. You administer the company's enterprise AI platforms, keep the SVP and the team's initiatives moving in sync, keep the roadmap current, and act as an early-warning system for what is changing at the AI frontier.

Early on the work is operations-heavy; your strategic voice is expected to grow as you automate the operations down. You are a force multiplier, not a support function.

Responsibilities: - Administer the company's enterprise AI platforms - Claude Enterprise, ChatGPT Enterprise, Gemini, and new tools as we adopt them - covering provisioning, access, RBAC, usage governance, and billing, and automate that administration down over time. - Keep the SVP of Innovation organized and ahead of schedule through prioritization, prep, and follow-through - you catch what would otherwise slip before it does. - Run the Innovation team's weekly operating rhythm and keep the roadmap current and trusted at all times. - Produce a weekly AI intelligence brief on what is shipping at the frontier and what the team should test. - Bring a point of view into strategy conversations and grow into a genuine strategic voice for the team. - Utilize and leverage Power Digital's Nova ecosystem as it relates to your department. - Other applicable or related duties as assigned.

Role Requirements: 2-4 years of experience; early-career with an unusually high ceiling and a fast learning rate. AI-native - you use Claude, ChatGPT, and Gemini daily and have real intuition for what they can and cannot do. This is the non-negotiable bar. A strong organizer who makes chaos legible and closes loops without being chased.

A clear writer and systems thinker who holds a point of view. Comfortable being the least experienced person in the room and still adding value. Meaningful daily overlap with U.S. Pacific hours (LATAM timezones ideal); remote, open to international candidates. Bonus: you have built something with AI - an agent, a workflow, or a shipped side project.

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) - Enterprise AI platform access and provisioning requests resolved within one business day, fully documented. - Admin time trending down quarter over quarter as workflows get automated. - Weekly AI intelligence brief shipped on time, every week. - Roadmap accurate and current at any given moment - never a scramble to update it. - Zero missed commitments or dropped follow-ups traceable to coordination gaps.

Most Important Things (MITs) - Be the reason the Innovation team's operations run without friction. - Keep the SVP focused on the highest-leverage work by owning everything beneath it. - Turn AI platform administration into a system that mostly runs itself. - Act as an early-warning system for what is changing in AI - surface it before it is obvious. - Earn a real voice in strategy by being right, useful, and fast.

The Procurement & Strategic Partnerships (PSP) team at Zoox builds the sourcing, contracting, and supplier relationships that keep our autonomous vehicle mission moving forward. We work at the intersection of operations, finance, and technology, bringing the same rigor and care to procurement that we bring to the vehicles we build. You'll join a team that values ownership, clear communication, and continuous improvement.

As Zoox scales, so does the complexity of sourcing and managing the services that support our business. In this role, you'll take on a variety of responsibilities, from supporting the deployment of a new business process outsourcing (BPO) relationship to helping drive the process improvements that make procurement work better for everyone at Zoox.

You'll have the opportunity to build from the ground up, deepen your knowledge of enterprise procurement operations, and grow your program and project management skills along the way.

Support the deployment and day-to-day oversight of a Managed Service Provider (MSP) BPO engagement covering offshore BuyDesk, sourcing support, supplier management, and contracting support.

Help build standard operating procedures (SOPs), governance, and escalation workflows for the BPO relationship.

Track and manage key performance indicators (KPIs) and service-level agreements (SLAs) to hold the BPO accountable for service quality.

Participate in procurement operations improvement projects that streamline how the business sources, buys, and manages suppliers.

Partner with stakeholders across Zoox to translate their requests into practical, scalable solutions

Manage multiple projects at once, prioritizing your time and resources as needs shift.

Use Procure-to-Pay (P2P) platforms such as Zip and Ariba to support requisitions, purchase orders, and invoice workflows across day-to-day procurement operations

Track record of converting stakeholder pain points into practical, scalable solutions

Experience managing multiple projects at once, prioritizing time and resources across competing priorities

Experience supporting the deployment and day-to-day operation of procurement-support delivery covering areas such as BuyDesk, sourcing support, supplier management, and contracting support, including implementing SOPs, program coordination, escalation workflows, and KPI/SLA management

Practical, hands-on experience with Procure-to-Pay (P2P) platforms, including requisition, purchase order, and invoice workflows

College degree with a concentration in a relevant field such as supply chain, business, or operations

At least 5 years of experience in and around corporate procurement

Experience with commercial procurement AI solutions

As a Commercial Operations Analyst at Zoox, you will help build and run the operational engine that drives our commercial P&L. Sitting at the center of our commercial business, you will turn pricing, promotions, and demand signals into the day-to-day and week-to-week decisions that move our growth and profitability targets—and stand up the rigor and rhythm that lets us manage those levers as we scale.
This is a high-ownership role for someone who is equally comfortable in the data and in the operating cadence of a fast-moving business.

You will partner closely with Product, Data Science, Fleet Operations, and Finance to translate complex commercial dynamics into clear actions, while helping establish the foundational processes that a growing Central Market Management team will be built on.

It is ideal for a technical, structured operator who is energized by ambiguity and excited to shape how an autonomous mobility business is run.

Run strategic pricing and promotions operations—standing up and owning the recurring processes to make, monitor, and evaluate pricing and promo decisions, and continuously assess how our commercial systems are performing.
Own the weekly rhythm of commercial health monitoring, building the metrics, reporting, and review cadences (e.g., market and system health, experiment readouts) that surface issues and guide lever decisions across the business.
Partner with Finance to translate commercial systems outputs and decisions into P&L impact, helping connect pricing, promos, and demand actions to cost, profit, and bookings outcomes.
Translate supply-demand dynamics into operational inputs—working with Fleet Orchestration and Fleet
Operations to inform parameterization, vehicle-hour targets, and demand management across waitlist, gating, and dynamic pricing.
Synthesize messy operational and financial data into clear, decision-ready recommendations and narratives for cross-functional partners and leadership.

6+ years of experience in a quantitative, high-output role—e.g., analytics, data science, strategy & operations, management consulting, investment banking, or a comparable operating role (ideally within mobility, logistics, marketplaces, or tech).
Strong technical foundation, with proficiency in SQL and Excel/Sheets and the ability to independently pull, structure, and analyze large, disparate datasets; comfort writing Python (or similar) to accelerate analysis is expected.
A degree in a quantitative or technical discipline (e.g., economics, finance, data science, engineering, or a related field); advanced degrees (MS or MBA) welcome.
Structured, hypothesis-driven problem solver who goes beyond surface metrics to understand underlying drivers, with strong analytical rigor and a high bar for accuracy in data that informs business and leadership decisions.
Ability to distill complex analysis into concise storytelling and to operate effectively across functions in an ambiguous, fast-changing environment.

Experience standing up new operational processes, metrics, or reporting rhythms from scratch (vs. running an established playbook).
Familiarity with pricing, promotions, demand/supply forecasting, or marketplace economics.
Experience with data visualization tools (Looker, etc.) and/or advanced analytics tooling (Python, R, Databricks).

Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.
Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

ElevenLabs is scaling fast – new enterprise customers, new products, new markets. The Billing Operations Specialist is the person who makes sure every deal that closes is reflected correctly in our systems.
This is an operational ownership role, sitting at the intersection of Sales, Customer Success, Finance, and Engineering – responsible for the full billing lifecycle of our enterprise accounts, from provisioning a new customer on day one to cleanly closing out a churned account. You'll resolve discrepancies before customers notice them, catch configuration drift before it becomes a revenue problem, and build the processes that make billing feel invisible to everyone else.
The ideal person is someone who is obsessive about accuracy, comfortable navigating ambiguity, and energized (not frustrated) by the complexity of managing billing at scale across hundreds of accounts.
Provisioning
Translate closed-won deals from Salesforce into correctly configured subscriptions in our billing platforms, such as Stripe – pricing plan, billing interval, contract start date, trial periods, discounts
Own the reconciliation between executed order forms and what's been requested for provisioning; work with Sales and Legal to resolve any gaps
Partner with Engineering to identify automation opportunities and build guardrails that make provisioning faster and more accurate over time
Subscription & account management
Process mid-cycle changes and manage renewal mechanics – upgrades, downgrades, seat changes, plan switches, and so on.
Handle offboarding cleanly: close subscriptions, issue final invoices or credits, ensure no residual billing
Resolve invoice discrepancies raised by customers or flagged by the Customer Success team – incorrect amounts, missing credits, misapplied discounts
Revenue integrity
Run periodic audits of active subscriptions to verify billing matches contracted terms
Identify and remediate ghost subscriptions, duplicate customers, and orphaned invoices
Support month-end and quarter-end close by reconciling billing platforms with Finance's records
Surface pricing or configuration anomalies to relevant teams.
Location
This role is remote-first, so it can be executed from anywhere in the United States, however the ability to operate in EST, CST, or PST timezones is required.
